findings.description: A second, tracked, stale copy of the fenced routing block still ships at the repository root. It is the pre-port 87-line version (last touched at 2f17deb, CRLF line endings), and it contains exactly the three defect classes this phase exists to eliminate: host-specific probes ('reading `.claude/skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md`' at :31, '`.claude/plans/`' at :56, '`.claude/settings.json`' at :83), seven completely ungated companion routes ('→ Invoke `/office-hours` (gstack)' at :12 etc. — the R1 class defect), and an unconditional `.advanced-plans/specs/` override under 'Superpowers Preference Overrides' (:53-58) with no manifest gate — the precise ACC-05 failure mode. The evidence file's loop-002-2 section states 'There is now exactly one routing block text in the repository'; that claim is false as of the current tree. The evidence removed the SETUP.md abridged copy for exactly this reason and missed this one. Mitigating: `project_ops.py:44` sets ROUTING_SOURCE to the canonical skill-dir path, this file is not listed in tests/packaging/required-sources.txt, and no README/SETUP/ARCHITECTURE/DESIGN-RATIONALE text points a user at it — so installed behaviour is unaffected. The risk is a human or agent finding an identically-named file at a more obvious path and installing the wrong text.
findings.evidence: `diff .claude/skills/setup-with-claude/references/claude-md-routing.md references/claude-md-routing.md` -> 1,213c1,87 (wholly different). `file references/claude-md-routing.md` -> 'with CRLF line terminators'; canonical is pure LF. `git ls-files references/` shows it is tracked. `grep -n '\.claude/' references/claude-md-routing.md` -> 3 hits at :31, :56, :83; the same grep on the canonical file -> zero hits.
findings.recommendation: Delete `references/claude-md-routing.md` (and audit `references/settings-snippet.json` alongside it), or replace its contents with a one-line pointer to the canonical file as was done for SETUP.md. Add a packaging check asserting that exactly one file in the repository contains the `aaw-routing:begin` marker as a live block rather than as quoted documentation.

findings.description: The behavioural half of SP-1, SP-2, ACC-04, ACC-05 and the Spike/Bounded negative rests entirely on the project's own narrative. The fixtures (`with-ap`, `without-ap`, `all-installed-2`, `only-superpowers`, `broken-manifest`), the ACC-RESULT.md reports, the worker transcripts and the pre/post hashes are not preserved anywhere in the repository or on disk — a filesystem search under the temp roots and ~/Coding found none of them. The evidence quotes worker output verbatim (e.g. 'Global gstack skills exist at `~/.claude/skills/gstack/` but the project manifest does not confirm installation...'), but those quotations cannot be checked against a retained report. The artefact side of every one of these criteria IS independently inspectable and I inspected it; the run side is not re-derivable by any reviewer.
findings.evidence: `find` over %TEMP%, /tmp and ~/Coding for all-installed*/only-superpowers/broken-manifest/with-ap/without-ap returned nothing. `git ls-files | grep -i 'acc-result|transcript'` returned nothing. `.advanced-plans/evidence/` contains only the twelve narrative markdown files.
findings.recommendation: For behavioural gates, commit the fixture manifest, the envelope, the resulting ACC-RESULT.md and the before/after hash lists under `.advanced-plans/evidence/<date>-<loop>/` so a later reviewer can re-read the primary record rather than the narrative about it.

findings.description: The recorded single-harness limitation is real and is correctly left open, but it is not disqualifying for any stated criterion. It touches five: 'SP-1 holds', 'SP-2 holds', 'ACC-05', the amended 'SP-2 attaches to the Architectural path only ... tested, not asserted', and by extension ACC-04. My reasoning for closing rather than failing on it: (a) no criterion in the plan or the amendment names a harness or requires multi-harness coverage, so failing on it would be reviewer-invented scope; (b) the measured harness is opencode reading AGENTS.md, i.e. the NON-native case — the block was authored in a Claude Code repository, so the harder direction is the one that was measured, and the F2 context probe demonstrated the block reaches a non-Claude harness automatically before the first message, which is the premise the whole zero-patch design rests on; (c) the delivery mechanism is an instruction file, which is advisory by construction for every harness, so 'measured on all harnesses' is a fidelity statistic, not a correctness gate. The countervailing fact is that adherence was NOT total even on the measured harness — round 5 ignored the block entirely, giving four of five with-ap rounds — so the phase closes with a mechanism proven to work and a fidelity figure known to be below 100%.
findings.evidence: .advanced-plans/evidence/2026-08-26-superpowers-port.md:818-822 ('all seven ACC rounds ... comes from the opencode harness'); :447-460 (the F2 context probe showing AGENTS.md is auto-loaded by opencode); :461-464 ('the block was applied in four of the five with-ap rounds that produced a result').
findings.recommendation: Carry the open item forward as a named phase-6 todo with a concrete acceptance test (same three installer-built fixtures, one envelope, run under `claude` and `codex`) rather than as prose in a closed phase's evidence file.

findings.description: Two acceptance checks were reinterpreted AFTER the run that they judge, by the same party that produced the result. loop-002-5's 'grep the whole output for .advanced-plans -> zero hits' was narrowed post-run to mean 'every file the worker produced, not the transcript'; loop-002-4's 'assert the Architectural terminal state invoked phase planning' was reinterpreted post-run as 'named phase planning as the handover, gave the manifest as its reason, and produced NO writing-plans plan document'. Both amendments are labelled 'AMENDED 2026-08-26, after the run', both carry a substantive argument, and both are defensible on the merits — a transcript must quote `.advanced-plans` while reasoning about a block that mentions it, and a fixture has no live `/new-phase` to execute. The loop-002-4 reinterpretation also ADDED two assertions rather than only removing one. The process concern stands regardless of merit: an unmet check was redefined by the measured party after measurement, and neither redefinition was put to an independent reviewer at the moment it was made.
findings.evidence: .advanced-plans/phases/phase-5/loops.md, loop-002-4 checks ('AMENDED 2026-08-26, after the run. "Invoked phase planning" cannot mean a slash command actually executing...') and loop-002-5 checks ('AMENDED 2026-08-26, after the run. "The whole output" is every file the worker produced, not the transcript.').
findings.recommendation: Require that any check amended after the run it judges be countersigned by the loop's cross-model reviewer before the loop is marked complete, or be re-run under the amended wording from a clean fixture — the R1 re-prove did the latter and is the right precedent.

findings.description: The amended criterion 'SP-4a is absent from the fork' is satisfied on the prepared mirror branch, not on the fork as it exists. `origin/main` is still fde9f97 and still carries all four intents; `git diff <merge-base> origin/main --stat` still shows the two-file net patch (skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md, skills/using-superpowers/SKILL.md, 73 insertions). The phase plan explicitly places publishing outside the controller's authority ('Not authorised by this amendment'), so this is in-scope-and-deferred rather than a failure — but the criterion as worded reads as a statement about the fork, and the true statement is about a local branch that nobody outside this machine can see.
findings.evidence: In C:/Users/mharvey2/Coding/superpowers: `git rev-parse --short origin/main` -> fde9f97; `git diff --stat f2cbfbe origin/main` -> 'skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md | 61 ++, skills/using-superpowers/SKILL.md | 22 +, 2 files changed, 73 insertions(+), 10 deletions(-)'. `git rev-list --left-right --count origin/main...mirror/upstream-2026-08-26` -> 4 241.
findings.recommendation: Reword the criterion to 'SP-4a is absent from the prepared mirror, which the operator publishes with one reviewed command', and carry the push (`git push origin mirror/upstream-2026-08-26:main --force-with-lease`) as an explicit open item on the phase-5 handoff rather than a paragraph inside the evidence file.

findings.description: loop-002-2's check was amended MID-loop from 'grep the block for plannotator -> zero hits' to 'every mention of Plannotator in the block is an explicit do-not-use instruction'. This is the implementer changing a check their own artefact would otherwise have failed. I judge it legitimate rather than post-hoc softening, for a reason I verified independently: the plan's own criterion is about the companion-tools RECOMMENDATION, and the recommendation (claude-md-routing.md:186-192) does not name Plannotator — the two mentions (:110, :194-196) are both prohibitions. The stated reason (upstream advanced-planning still ships companion-detection/SKILL.md naming Plannotator, so an agent reading both files must be told which is current) is a real disambiguation need, and both loop-002-7 reviewers subsequently read the block without objecting to it.
findings.evidence: claude-md-routing.md:110 ('Note: plannotator was deprecated on 2026-08-26. Do not route to it or detect it.') and :194-196 ('Plannotator is **not** part of this stack... Do not recommend, detect, install, or route to it'). `grep -i plannotator` returns exactly those two sites; neither sits inside the Companion Tools recommendation paragraphs at :186-192.
findings.recommendation: No action. Recorded so the supersession is visible rather than silent.

findings.description: Audit of the evidence file's numeric and mechanical claims against the artefacts. Every one I could re-derive held. 'Eleven sites' — reproduces exactly: the predicate-definition line, the default-deny catch-all, front-door rules 1-7, Companion Tools, and the Closing Instruction = 11 R1-related sites in commit 911a6ba. '178 -> 213 lines, still pure LF' — `git show 553d926:<file> | wc -l` = 178, current = 213, CR byte count = 0. 'packaging 4/4 and idempotency 56/56' — I re-ran `bash tests/packaging/run-all.sh` myself: 'idempotency: PASS - 56/56 checks', 'packaging: PASS - 4/4 checks'. "grep '→ Invoke|→ Use the' returns nothing" — zero hits. 'Gate phrasing appears three times for gstack, six for Advanced Planning, once for superpowers' — 3, 6, 1 exactly. '`grep -c MUTANT project_ops.py` returns 0' — returns 0. 'the upstream default at skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md:100 and :206' — both lines carry `docs/superpowers/specs/`. 'writing-plans default of docs/superpowers/plans/' — upstream writing-plans/SKILL.md:18. The controller's adjudication of the codex-vs-Qwen contradiction is also independently correct: the diff of 911a6ba shows rules 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 7 were ungated before the fix, so codex's claim was true and Qwen's sentence was false. One claim did NOT hold: 'exactly one routing block text in the repository' (see the major finding).
findings.evidence: Commands and outputs as listed; all re-run by this reviewer against the working tree at 911a6ba plus four untracked files.

summary: MODEL: claude-opus-5[1m] (Claude Opus 5, 1M context). I read plan.md (both the original Success Criteria and the 2026-08-26 Amendment), loops.md in full including loop-002-7's resolution field, the 825-line port evidence file, and claude-md-routing.md line by line; then went to the artefacts rather than the claims. Independently verified: the routing block is 213 lines, pure LF, with zero .claude//.cursor//.opencode/ probes and the manifest predicate at :14-34; SP-1 at :146-150, SP-2 (Architectural-only, with the over-process warning) at :130-136 and :152-156, SP-3 at :138-144 with a prose fallback, SP-4a at :186-192 naming Advanced Planning and never Plannotator in a recommendation; all eleven R1 gate sites present and `grep '→ Invoke|→ Use the'` returning nothing. In the superpowers checkout I confirmed mirror/upstream-2026-08-26 and upstream/main are the SAME commit (b36e082) with `git diff --quiet` exit 0 and rev-list 0 in both directions, the backup tag on fde9f97, the 4/241 divergence, and the Three Paths router present verbatim at upstream/main:22-52 — a zero-diff mirror is a stronger proof of router integrity than a section diff. I re-ran tests/packaging/run-all.sh myself: idempotency 56/56, packaging 4/4, matching the evidence exactly. Commit ordering confirms the matrix and its gate (14:10, 14:15) preceded the first implementation commit (14:34). On the four judgement calls asked of me: (1) the both-directions criteria are supported artefactually in both directions and behaviourally in both directions, but only by narrative — the fixtures are gone; (2) the single-harness limitation touches SP-1, SP-2, ACC-04, ACC-05 and the Architectural-only criterion and is a limitation the phase can close with, not disqualifying, because no criterion names a harness and the measured harness is the harder non-native one — though adherence was 4/5 even there; (3) the supersessions are legitimate and mostly strengthening (empty-tree-diff is stricter than first-commit-is-upstream; SP-3 was added to scope, not dropped), with two post-run check reinterpretations by the measured party that are defensible on merits but were not independently countersigned; (4) the evidence's numeric claims all reproduce except one. That exception is the reason this is not a clean pass: a tracked, stale, CRLF copy of the routing block still sits at references/claude-md-routing.md carrying three .claude/ probes, seven ungated routes and an unconditional .advanced-plans/specs/ override — the exact R1 and ACC-05 failure modes — while the evidence claims exactly one block text exists in the repository. It does not reach installed behaviour (project_ops.py reads the skill-dir path) so it does not fail a criterion, but it contradicts the record and is a live footgun. Verdict: pass_with_findings. Isolation disclosure: I did not open .advanced-plans/gate-verdicts/; one repository-wide grep incidentally surfaced text from files in that directory, which I discarded without reading or using — no criterion below is judged on it, and no criterion required it.

Named checks observed passing include 'the user's own AGENTS.md content survives verbatim', 'a second install is byte-identical', 'installing again changes neither file', 'the two files carry byte-identical block text', 'uninstall returns AGENTS.md to the bytes it started with', 'a half fence in AGENTS.md exits 3', and 'CLAUDE.md is byte-identical - checked before anything was written'. The last is the two-pass uninstall ordering, which I confirmed in the implementation at tests/packaging/project_ops.py:137-160 (all files scanned for incomplete markers before any is written), and the evidence's mutation testing is corroborated by `grep -c MUTANT project_ops.py` -> 0.
